content.text: In the same way that you can pass a closure *to* a function, you can get closures returned *from* a function too.
The syntax for this is a bit confusing at first, because it uses `->` twice: once to specify your function’s return value, and a second time to specify your closure’s return value.
To try this out, we’re going to write a `travel()` function that accepts no parameters, but returns a closure. The closure that gets returned must be called with a string, and will return nothing.

title: Returning closures from functions
question: This code is valid Swift – true or false?
hint: Make sure the returned closure accepts the right parameters and returns the right data type, if any.

wrong.reason: The parameter to `makeSharer()` needs to have a name.
`makeCodeGenerator()` says it will return a closure, but instead returns a string.
`mealProducer()` says it will return a closure that accepts an integer and returns a string, but it returns a closure that accepts a string and returns nothing.
`paintingMaker()` says it will return a closure that accepts a string and returns nothing, but the closure it returns accepts no parameters.
`catchPokemon()` says it will return an empty tuple, not a closure.
The return value of `makeGame()` needs to be written with parentheses around the parameter type: `(Int) -> Void`.
